content:
alex: heads up — seeing non-deterministic failures in the QA eval after upgrading int8 kernels. same seed and sampling config but different token at pos 12 across runs

maria: which test and run id? link?

alex: qa/bert-qa-smoke, dashboard: https://redwood-inf/qa/2103. local run passes, CI run fails. example diffs attached — one output says "on monday" vs "monday" (tiny but fails exact-match). suspect something with prefix handling and sampler alignment.

sam: that rings a bell — if the RNG stream isn't anchored across kernel swaps / worker handoffs you can get a one-token drift. did we change continuous-batching behavior with the new kernel?

jen: config used: `temp=0.0 top_p=0.95 sampling=multinomial seed=42 batch_size=8 resume_policy=kv_resume quant_profile=int8-fast`

alex: pasted a short trace: ```
[runner] seed=42 rng_pos=128 kernels=[fp16, int8_fast, int8_slow]
[worker-3] consumed_prefix=7 after_kv_restore rng_pos=135
[next_token] sampled_index=17
```

eval-bot: CI job 2103456701: eval-runner-smoke failed (2/105 checks). failing shards: qa/bert-int8-fast-path, qa/bert-int8-slow-path

maria: ok — action items: 1) add lightweight rng checkpoints (hash of next N randoms) around kernel/context switches, 2) instrument tokens_consumed per worker at resume, 3) add a CI smoke that rotates workers/kernels to try to catch drift.

sam: i can repro locally by forcing kernel order swap during a long prefix. quick hack: force `kernels=[int8_fast,int8_slow,fp16]` on one worker and you get off-by-one in sampled stream. prob cause: rng counter not advanced for cached kv tokens when switching to quantized codepath.

jen: proposed fix in runner: persist an explicit `rng_counter` on the request context and increment deterministically for every generated token and for tokens skipped during prefix replay. i'll open a tiny PR that wires that into the sampling primitive. also add a unit that simulates a kernel swap and asserts identical outputs.

alex: opened issue #4121 with repro script and minimal traces, assigned to @jen and @sam. linking logs: https://redwood-inf/logs/4121. tagging for postmortem if this doesn't land before next release :crossed_fingers:

maria: additional telemetry idea — emit a 64-bit hash of the first 64 RNG outputs per request as a quick drift detector. small and cheap to compare across runs.

sam: ack, will prototype the hash in the sampler shim. if it gets salty we can gate an alert.

jen: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runner/pull/1982 — adds rng_counter + kernel-swap unit test. requesting review from @sam and @alex.

alex: testing PR locally now. thanks all.
